$comment: Tassel's tools, in the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions format (also accepted by Ollama and ds4). `tools` is sent to the model as is by clawer.desk.chat.TasselChatService; `policy` is not sent -- it is what the API does with each call. The model only proposes: TasselToolExecutor validates every change against the same rules as the desk forms, records it in desk.chat_action, and then applies it or holds it for the user to confirm. lookup_us_federal_data is the one read: TasselFederalLookup answers it, nothing is recorded or changed, and its caveats travel with the chat response. Enums must match DeskTargetService / DeskTaskService (TasselToolsContractTest), and the names of the tools that change something must match V004's allow-list.

function.name: update_target_list
function.description: Change the user's list of target schools when they clearly say so in this conversation: they decide to apply somewhere, a school's status changes (they submitted, were admitted, deferred, rejected, withdrew), or they drop a school. Do not call it for a school they are only wondering about ("maybe", "what about"), and do not call it for a school you suggested. Adding a school is applied at once and can be undone; changing a stage or removing a school is shown to the user as a proposal to confirm.

action.description: add: a school that is not on the list yet. update: change the stage, round, deadline or band of a listed school. remove: take a listed school off the list.

targetEntityId.description: For update and remove: the id of the school in the targets listed in your context. Null for add. Never guess an id.

universityName.description: For add: the school exactly as the user named it. CrawlerNest links it to its university records only on an exact name match and otherwise keeps the user's wording. Null for update and remove.

programmeName.description: The programme or major, if the user named one.

stage.description: The stage the user says the school is now at.

applicationRound.description: The round, only if the user said which.

deadline.description: YYYY-MM-DD, only if the user stated the date. Do not supply a deadline from memory: published deadlines change every year.

userBand.description: Only if the user themself called the school a reach, target or safety. Never infer it.

reason.description: The user's words that asked for this change, quoted or closely paraphrased. Shown to the user beside the change.

function.name: create_action_task
function.description: Add an action item to the user's task list when they mention something they need to do, especially one with a date ("the supplement is due Nov 1", "I should email my counselor this week"). One call per action. If the date is ambiguous ("next Friday" near a month end, a date with no year that could be either), ask before calling. Applied at once and can be undone.

title.description: A short imperative: "Submit MIT supplement", "Email Ms. Chen about the recommendation".

dueDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD, resolved against the date and time zone in your context. Must not be in the past. Null when the user gave no date.

priority.description: high only for something due within seven days or that the user called urgent; otherwise null (normal).

category.description: One word or two: Essay, Testing, Recommendations, Application, Financial aid.

targetEntityId.description: The listed school this task is for, if any, from the targets in your context.

sourceQuote.description: The user's words that this task comes from, quoted.

function.name: generate_narrative_themes
function.description: Store one or two narrative themes: a short line that names the thread running through the user's experiences (for example "The Builder Who Teaches"), drawn only from what the user has told you or written in their drafts. Call it when the user asks what their story is, or at the end of a brainstorming session that has produced enough concrete material -- at least two distinct experiences with specific details. Themes are saved as suggestions; the user accepts or dismisses each one.

title.description: Four to eight words, concrete, no clichés (avoid "passionate leader", "lifelong learner").

summary.description: Two or three sentences, addressed to the user, saying what the thread is and which experiences carry it.

traits.description: One to five short trait labels the evidence supports.

evidence.description: Where the theme comes from. Each quote must be copied verbatim from the user's own message or essay; CrawlerNest checks it and drops any it cannot find. A theme left with no evidence is not stored.

sourceRef.description: For essay_review, the review id from your context. Null for chat_message.

function.name: lookup_us_federal_data
function.description: Read the US federal figures (College Scorecard and IPEDS: admission rate, test score ranges, cost, net price, completion, earnings, enrollment) for one school on the student's list, when they ask about one of those for a US school. Reads only; changes nothing. Returns each figure with its own period and status, and the caveats you must pass on. Many schools have no record: outside the US, or not matched.

targetEntityId.description: The id of the school on the student's list, from the context. A school not on the list must be added with update_target_list first.

update_target_list.universityMatching: exact normalized name or alias only; otherwise kept as customName. Never fuzzy (CLAUDE.md, entity resolution traps).

generate_narrative_themes.outcome: stored as status 'suggested'; only the user can accept
generate_narrative_themes.evidenceCheck: each quote must occur verbatim in the named source; unmatched quotes are dropped, and a theme with none left is rejected

lookup_us_federal_data.outcome: read only: not recorded in desk.chat_action, no confirm or undo
lookup_us_federal_data.lookup: the target's linked warehouse university only; a target with no linked university, or a university with no matched UNITID, has no figures. Never by name.
lookup_us_federal_data.caveats: every successful lookup adds its caveats to the chat response, and the desk shows them under the reply
